title: Bitwise complement rejects booleans but accepts integers and strings

ground_truth.statement: Bitwise complement accepts integers and byte strings, but neither boolean value is a supported operand. Both true and false throw TypeError at the operator. Integer and string controls prove complement results independently; booleans are not implicitly treated as zero and one here.

provenance.derivation: Independent minimal fixture based on the invalidBooleanBitwiseNot lead. A native boolean parameter replaces the literal, and native integer/string controls expose the operator domain. No upstream program body copied.

notes: Expectations follow native operator semantics, not analyzer observations. The explicit mixed return avoids prescribing a result type to an operation that always throws. Mago 1.58.2 stays silent, a measured false negative. PHPStan 2.3.1 and Psalm 6.20.1 report the required error. Pzoom's pinned revision attempts this check but has mandatory builtin-stub scan errors; its run is a tool_error, not a quality verdict.
